flags: No cached history identifies the modern byway’s builders, campaigners or designation date, and no drive time is given. Overview uses the documented transport history of its communities without claiming these railroads created the highway.
Moments follow the official south-to-north itinerary, reversing the material strip’s mile order. The corridor uses several numbered highways; it is not entirely Highway 9.

Alabama Byways calls Piedmont depot an 1888 building, while Piedmont Wikipedia calls it an 1867 facility and the station article says it served Southern Railway from 1868. Building date and early operator conflation are omitted; the 1868 Selma, Rome, and Dalton arrival is attributed to the byway account through evidence.
Canyon Rim Parkway is an additional drive, not AL 35. Sources give 22 and 23 miles for it; neither length is repeated. No canyon-depth superlative or longest-river claim is reused.
All current moment subjects and supported claims are retained or developed; no current claim required dropping as wholly unsupported. Centre’s county-seat naming story was cut for narrative focus.
The Fort Payne article conflates the mill and depot in one sentence; neither that identity nor the conflicting worldwide sock share is reused. The U.S. share is explicitly historical.
